_spec.law: Facts resolve to the original verified claim record. A layout rebuild does not reverify reporting.

dek.text: TACC retired Frontera in October. A UT Southwestern lab says a simulation that ran on {{number:c8:1}} Frontera CPU nodes got almost the same speed on eight Vista GPU nodes.

introduction.text: [The Texas Advanced Computing Center at UT Austin retired Frontera in October 2026, after the machine had run more than eight million jobs](c1). [For most of its service life it was the fastest academic supercomputer in the United States](c3), [and its run of more than seven years was the longest of any TACC system, the center's executive director said](c2).

[The center gave that account in its report on a September symposium for Texas researchers](c18), [which drew a record turnout](c19). [One of the speakers was Jose Rizo-Rey of UT Southwestern Medical Center](c7), whose description of moving a large simulation onto newer hardware is the clearest measure the account offers of what the change of machines means for a working lab.

paragraphs.text: [Rizo-Rey said his group typically ran a {{number:c8}} million atom simulation on {{number:c8:1}} CPU nodes of Frontera at {{number:c8:2}} nanoseconds of simulated time per day](c8). [On TACC's Vista system, he said, eight GPU nodes gave him almost the same speed](c9).

[He said getting there took a lot of optimization of GROMACS, with help from TACC staff](c10). [GROMACS describes itself as free and open source software for high performance molecular dynamics](c33). The comparison is his own spoken account in the center's release. It is not a published benchmark, and the release gives no simulated time per day for Vista.

[The NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchip is the processor for the majority of Vista's {{number:c25:1}} compute nodes, TACC has said](c25), [and it pairs a Grace CPU with a Hopper GPU](c26). [Each Frontera node, by TACC's description of its expansion, held two Intel Xeon Platinum 8280 processors](c30).

[Rizo-Rey studies synaptic transmission](c15). [His simulations contain a vesicle, a flat bilayer and four SNARE protein complexes](c11), [the proteins that let vesicles fuse with their target membranes](c12).

[The key concept the simulations and analysis point to is that the SNAREs act as a local detergent](c13), [catalyzing the mixing of the hydrophobic interiors of the two membranes](c14). The account does not say whether that finding has been published in a journal, and it gives no figures for how the simulated fusion compares with experiments.

[Frontera's successor, Horizon, the centerpiece of the NSF Leadership-Class Computing Facility, has entered its first phase of early operations](c4). [The center's executive director said its power infrastructure is complete and an exabyte capacity storage system is in place](c5), [and the initial deployment of its AI focused hardware is under way](c6).

[A researcher from the Oden Institute who had early access said Horizon is entering full production soon](c22). The account gives no date for full production and no figure for how many of Vista's or Horizon's nodes researchers can expect to use. [More than {{number:c23:1}} U.S. researchers have used TACC's systems since {{number:c23}}](c23).
